name: The New India Assurance Company Ltd
title: The New India Assurance Company Ltd - 540769 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Insurer's FY26 combined ratio hit 122.57% on wage-revision charges (116.67% ex-wage), with motor TP and OD ICRs worsening; management guides motor to single-digit growth and better ratios, but commentary on pricing is competitive and unhedged on rate relief.

triggers.label: Motor TP ICR 108.17% → 113.86%
triggers.quote: Motor TP also saw a worsening of the ICR from 108.17% to 113.86%.

triggers.label: Q4 fire premium degrowth -4.33%
triggers.quote: Q4 saw a reduction of 4.33% degrowth. The reason for this being that the market was highly competitive, the rates literally crashing in the property market.

triggers.label: Motor growth single digit, combined ratio to fall
triggers.quote: On Motor, I think it will be a single digit growth. We will not be very aggressive on Motor.

triggers.label: Motor discounts rising every quarter
triggers.quote: No, it has gone up. It has been increasingly going up over every quarter in the last year.

guidance.quote: On Motor, I think it will be a single digit growth. We will not be very aggressive on Motor.
It would be a single digit for Motor, double digit for the entire book.
I think the overall ratios will also show a reducing trend in the current fiscal.

red_flags.label: Combined ratio 122.57% incl. wage revision
red_flags.quote: The combined ratio was reported at 122.57%.

red_flags.label: Motor TP premium rate stagnant, awards rising
red_flags.quote: The reason being that the much-awaited premium increase has still not happened, which we are awaiting for.

red_flags.quote: It has been increasingly going up over every quarter in the last year.

evasions.quote: It will also be linked with our strategies fo r this portfolio recalibration.
when you talk about growth, it's also in context with the environment.

summary.headline: New India Assurance FY26 profit after tax rose 40% to INR 1,384 crore, but combined ratio worsened to 122.57% on wage-revision charges.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 GWP grew only 1.63% to INR 11,619 crore, reflecting competitive property pricing, while Indian domestic GDP grew 10.9% versus the industry's 9.3%. The full-year combined ratio rose to 122.57% (116.67% excluding the wage revision impact) as the company absorbed INR 3,525 crore of wage and family pension revision costs. Incurred claim ratio rose to 98.65% on Motor TP court awards, the Air India aviation loss, marine claims and NATCAT flood claims not fully recovered under reinsurance. Management guided to a Motor single-digit growth and double-digit overall growth in FY27, led by Health Retail.

vs 116.78% in FY25; 116.67% excluding wage revision (vs 115.34%)
vs INR 6,124 crore loss in FY25

segments.name: Health and PA
segments.commentary: 47.57% of book; premium up 12.62% in FY26 but only 2.58% in Q4. ICR improved to 99.05% from 100.98%, helped by TPA audits raised from 30% to 50%.

segments.name: Fire
segments.commentary: Premium up 10.76% in FY26 but down 4.33% in Q4 on property rate cuts. ICR rose to 76.54% from 71.20% on small NATCAT claims not fully reinsured.

segments.name: Motor OD
segments.commentary: Premium up only 2% in FY26 and 11.48% in Q4 after deliberate portfolio pruning. ICR worsened to 108.85% from 104.22%; management expects about a year to see impact.

segments.name: Motor TP
segments.commentary: Premium up 0.13% in FY26 with no tariff revision yet; ICR rose to 113.86% from 108.17% as court awards increased.

segments.name: Marine
segments.commentary: Premium up 11.43% in FY26 and 20.26% in Q4; ICR jumped to 86.74% from 53.74% on cargo claims and a general average claim.

segments.name: Crop
segments.commentary: Premium declined as inward crop reinsurance was not accepted; ICR rose to 96.15% from 81.02% on legacy claims.

segments.name: Other lines
segments.commentary: Premium up 12.48% in FY26 and 2.03% in Q4; ICR rose to 63.40% from 58.77%. Miscellaneous ex-crop grew about 26% per analyst question, driven by engineering, liability and surety bonds.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 industry growth in double digits; New India to grow double digits overall.
Motor growth to be single digit in FY27, with focus on profitability over volume.
Overall ratios expected to show a reducing trend in FY27 as Motor portfolio recalibration takes hold.
Motor mix target: private cars and two-wheelers to dominate; CVs above 7,500 cc to be reduced; two-wheelers to move toward double-digit share selectively.
Motor OD premium increases planned on selected segments; commissions and payouts to be adjusted dynamically in commercial lines.
Health Retail to be the primary growth driver under the 'GO RETAIL' mandate.
capex_capacity: Motor portfolio churn started from Q2 FY26; management says about another year is needed to reach the target mix.
IT infrastructure revamp nearing completion; all retail products online; mobile super apps for customers, intermediaries and surveyors launched.
Automated survey appointment and digital survey reports implemented.
Digital marketing and sales piloted for a few Health products, to be extended to other lines.
Bharat Maritime Pool operationalised with sovereign guarantee; company acting as lead insurer for P&I and hull risk.
demand_pricing: Industry GDP reached about INR 3.36 lakh crore in FY26, up 9.3%; New India's domestic share rose from 12.56% to 12.74%.
Segment market shares: Fire 17.56%, Marine 17.77%, Motor 9.91%, Health and PA 14.93%, other lines 15.13%.
Property rates fell sharply in H2 FY26 on competition, driving Fire Q4 degrowth.
Motor competition described as extremely competitive; discounts rising every quarter over the past year.
Motor sales recovered after GST rationalisation: private cars grew 17.8% and two-wheelers 21.5% in H2 FY26; Q4 growth was 16.3% and 24.7%.
Distribution mix (domestic): broker 35.79%, direct 30.13%, agency 25.91%, dealer 7.56%, bancassurance 0.61%.
Commissions cut across many lines including Health; reinsurance commissions increased. Q4 commission ratio fell to 9.53% from 11.17%.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the Motor portfolio course correction take, when will loss ratios fall, and will OD premiums be repriced?
qa_highlights.answer: Correction began in Q2 FY26 and needs about another year; overall ratios expected to fall in FY27. OD premium increases planned on selected segments. Competition remains extremely competitive with discounts rising each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the target Motor mix?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 mix: private cars 47.56%, commercial vehicles 45.60%, two-wheelers 6.79%. Plan to exit CVs above 7,500 cc and grow private cars and two-wheelers, with two-wheelers toward double digits selectively.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the commission ratio decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissions reduced across many lines including Health, and reinsurance commissions increased, so net commission moved in the company's favour.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 growth outlook and capital gains for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Double-digit growth expected for the company, with Motor at single digit. FY26 capital gains were about INR 5,477 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Where will Health and PA profitability go?
qa_highlights.answer: Health ICR reduced by about 2% and commission ratio cut, which management says significantly raised segment profitability; individual Health demand supported by 18% GST waiver.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is market share gain and how will underwriting discipline hold with faster growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth described as strategic, mainly retail; underwriting guidelines set by head office with strict periodic monitoring.

risks_watch: Combined ratio of 122.57% and ICR of 98.65%; watch whether ratios fall in FY27 as management guided.
Motor TP premium revision still pending while court awards rise; Motor OD ICR at 108.85%.
Wage revision and family pension costs (INR 3,525 crore in FY26; INR 597 crore absorbed in Q4) may weigh on future results.
Q4 GWP growth of 1.63% and Fire degrowth of 4.33% amid property rate cuts.
Long-run market share decline from about 19% (FY09) to 12.74% amid rising competition from new private insurers.
Solvency ratio fell to 1.84x from 1.91x; fair value of investments fell to INR 13,878 crore from INR 21,406 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, market leadership and Health profitability, but noticeably defensive on the 122.57% combined ratio and Motor losses, relying on a one-year timeline and general statements about discipline. Answers on pricing, commissions and competition were brief and lacked specific targets.
key_quotes: We have just started this course correction in Motor from the second quarter of this year.
It would be a single digit for Motor, double digit for the entire book.
We have reduced the ICR this year by 2% and also brought down the commission ratio.

growth.why: Management guides double-digit overall book growth in FY27 led by Health Retail and single-digit Motor growth, with a reducing combined-ratio trend, but no specific capacity, order or contract numbers back the guidance.
